column5: Promotes a one-off to a standing naming rule binding every name in the vocabulary, giving jn1.63 a rule instead of eight judgement calls
Removes the last workaround that would let the surface grow at a minor, so what it defines is the reach of the major-lock
Allocates the residual gap to the ADR's Consequences and keeps it out of the spec, deciding which audience is told what
Spans rule and feedback; higher-leverage taken -- extends the standing checklist refusal to cover its mechanised form, so no tool escapes it
Records that two gaps are not each other's remedy, fixing what the record says so the pair is not offered again
Rules that both halves of a source are recorded or neither, so a named counter-precedent cannot be manufactured into an invitation
Fixes which ticket discharges the routed finding and that the spec opening has two named feeders, correcting where a drafter must look
Spans rule and information flow; higher-leverage taken -- the standing rule that closed-ticket text is read as of its date, with erratum as the only remedy
Holds link integrity and provenance apart, so a detection claim is not read as the provenance claim the record denies
Re-sources the value's existence to a from-0.5.1 invariant and its shape to const-evaluability, replacing a void forcing ground
Sets the 1.0 scope boundary for enabling support: present sufficiency, nothing further owed, no new surface admitted
Fixes the effort's governing stance -- current-state-only by default, immutability only where a store or boundary forces it -- from which record decisions follow
Decides what the record renders: one derived direction, no second rendering of an edge the tool already computes
States the non-disturbance explicitly so a reader meeting two regimes does not read a general rule that was never made
Fixes one point on the boundary: a non-substantive edit never triggers the supersession machinery
Governs evolvability directly -- the public struct field set is major-locked, so growth costs a major
Lays the standing surface constraint as a property clause, striking the mechanism half the naming rule now forbids
Closes the 1.x additive-change surface: exactly three permitted additions, nothing else, one principle underneath
Fixes where an existing guarantee actually lives, so relaxing a Rust attribute cannot be misread as weakening a non-Rust promise
Discharges two items as already ruled by name, refusing a second rendering that could drift from the first
Lays down the two-tier design discipline -- refuse-at-open binds, inexpressibility preferred where affordable, never mandated
Fixes the applicability condition of the discipline to a marker the spec must carry anyway, minting no artefact
Puts the meta-rule outside the stranger-facing surface, so a consumer gets the outcomes and not the reasoning that produced them
Fixes the rule's reach as already covering consumer configuration, correcting a premise that would have reserved a governed case
Sets the standing test for when supersession fires: the decision's direction, never the diff
Adds the tie-breaker that closes the one movement escaping both prior rules -- scope narrowing or widening supersedes
Restricts who may produce a descriptor at all, taking the reversible direction while it is free
Fixes the actual reach of the verification: provenance is checked structurally, faithfulness is never a check that could fire
Makes the spec state the limit plainly, so a stranger can tell which guarantee they hold
Carves the named exception without which the derive-only rule is false on its face
Records that the documentation asserts a falsehood, so the rebuilder builds the guarantee rather than the wording
